chapter: New Orleans bands, Louis and the Lyric
title: Getting the John Robichaux job at the Lyric Theater
summary: Robichaux heard Zutty from outside the Cadillac and hired him; Willie Jackson and another rehearsed him on the chorus-girl kicks. The Lyric stood at Burgundy Street and shone a light on him.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: But then how long did this go at the Cadillac?
Well, it went on quite a while until old man Robichaux was standing outside listening at me play and that's how I got the job.
John. That's how, and Willie Jackson and Snooky would give me rehearsals on how the girls were going to kick and everything you know. Oh they had me really sharp and ready to go into the
Where abouts was the Lyric Theater?
It was the Burgundy and, oh, Burgundy and, it was right on a corner. Burgundy and (unintelligible).
Oh! Down in the Vieux Carre?

Yes. It was the next block, was the Palace Theater. That's where Ervin Le Claire and those guys were playing. And the drummer, Stein. He was a sensational drummer too. They shined the light on him. And that's what they used to do me at the Lyric, shine the light on me.
(REMAINDER OF FIRST TAPE ALMOST COMPLETELY INAUDIBLE. TYPIST DID NOT THINK WORTHWHILE TO TRY TO TRANSCRIBE).
* Lyric Theater- 201 Burgundy Street. viz- Rose & Souchon, New Orleans Jazz; A Family Album, p. 212 1967 ed.
